The Coalition That Can't Agree on Its Own Boss

Gadi Eisenkot wants Israelis to enjoy their beach vacation in Cyprus. His billboards near Larnaca airport say so directly: "Israelis, enjoy! You deserve it," followed by a second sign on the way home: "Landed? Had fun? Now come back and win!"

A Cypriot MEP is now demanding a ban on foreign election ads, which means Eisenkot has achieved something Netanyahu never managed: uniting Cypriots against Israeli politics.

Back home, the general-turned-candidate has bigger enemies than tourism regulators — namely, his own bloc. 

"A reality where a party leader with 8 to 10 seats demands the premiership is not appropriate," Eisenkot said, a line he's repeated for months, most recently aimed squarely at Naftali Bennett. 

Translation from campaign-speak: I have more mandates in the polls, so kindly step aside and let the man with the bigger poll number run the country.

Meanwhile, Yashar! just recruited Eliana Sachs, 25, model and social activist from Beer Sheva, who lost her mother and brother to an Iranian missile strike on the city, to run the party's youth wing. 

Eisenkot called her "the Israel of today — determined, values-driven, a true blend of action and spirit". Grief, rebranded as campaign strategy, is apparently the fastest-growing sector in Israeli politics this cycle.

And when Ynet's Moran Azoulai pressed him on his own record, Eisenkot didn't dodge — he doubled down: "As chief of staff I said that until the bodies of the fallen are returned, I won't approve bringing in workers from Gaza. 
Not one laborer entered from Gaza in all four years I served as chief of staff." A hard line delivered with the confidence of a man who knows exactly how many mandates that kind of sentence is worth in October.

So who's actually running this campaign — the candidate polling ahead of Netanyahu, or the grief, the guilt, and the billboards doing the polling for him?

Machu Picchu, a stunning remnant of the Inca Empire, features masterfully cut stone fitted together so precisely that not even a blade can slip between the blocks—all without using mortar. Perched high on a ridge above the Urubamba River, it’s thought to have served as a spiritual retreat, ceremonial center, or royal sanctuary.

Tucked into the Andes and embraced by the lush forests of the Amazon Basin, the site is part of a larger sacred network tied to celestial movements. Constructed 500 years ago without iron tools or the wheel, its architectural brilliance includes agricultural terraces and sophisticated water management systems.

Lost for centuries, it was brought back to light in 1911. Having escaped destruction during Spanish colonization, it stands today as a major destination for travelers—where ongoing efforts strive to balance access with long-term preservation.

🎙 Lut Desert’s scientific, tourism potential highlighted on UNESCO anniversary

📌 Tehran, IRNA – The Lut Desert, considered one of the hottest places on Earth, still holds many unexplored and pristine treasures. According to Iranian experts, it offers a valuable and unique potential for scientific research, education, and the development of nature-based tourism.

The four experts addressed a specialized meeting held virtually on the tenth anniversary of the inscription of the Lut Desert on the UNESCO World Heritage List on July 18. The meeting was organized by Tehran University’s International Desert Research Center and the Lut Desert World Heritage Site.
​
Nasser Mashhadi, a University of Tehran professor and geomorphology researcher, described the Lut Desert as a natural museum of wind and water processes, highlighting its unique geological features, including yardangs, known locally as kalouts, sand dunes, alluvial plains and rare armoured mud balls. He said the desert’s exceptional geomorphological diversity provides valuable opportunities for scientific research, education and the development of geotourism.
​
Hessam Ahmadi Birgani, a faculty member at the University of Urmia’s Faculty of Natural Resources, highlighted the economic and tourism potential of Iran’s sandy areas, noting that they cover about five million hectares of the country’s territory. He called for a shift in approach from viewing sand dunes as a “threat” to recognizing them as an “opportunity,” pointing to new industrial applications of sand as well as the potential of dark skies, desert silence and local community participation in developing sustainable tourism.
​
Hamidreza Naseri, a University of Tehran professor and head of the International Desert Research Center, presented the results of the first ground-based measurement of the Lut Desert’s surface temperature conducted July 18, 2022, saying that the findings confirmed satellite data and reinforced the Lut’s status as one of the hottest places on Earth and a natural laboratory for climate, geography and climate-change studies.
​
Mehran Maqsoudi, a University of Tehran professor and director of the Lut Desert World Heritage Site, highlighted the desert’s unique ecosystem, including heat- and drought-resistant plant species and animals adapted to its harsh climate, and described the Lut’s kalouts as the world’s tallest, longest and most continuous known yardangs.
​
Participants stressed the need for scientific management of tourism, empowerment of local communities, continuous monitoring of climate change and national and international cooperation to protect the world heritage site.

📝On the case against Durov📝
And the problem of perceiving facts

The recent news about the criminal prosecution of Telegram's creator is naturally perceived in the context of crude blockades and non-market mechanisms in the digital sphere. But the situation has several dimensions nonetheless.

Back in spring, we wrote that law enforcement agencies have quite logical demands of the platform — to work with them at least roughly in the same volume as with the special services of other countries. After Durov's arrest in Paris in 2024, the balance began to shift even more, and not in Russia's favor.

One can recall the bans on channels affiliated with Wagner PMC or the African Corps — now Telegram requires even their advertising to be removed. No matter how you look at it, such zeal is not observed toward "kompromat" bots and especially Ukrainian resources, and there is no talk of storing Russian citizens' data in Russia.

📌Of course, it is very difficult to refuse certain requests when living in countries under Western jurisdiction, where the platform's servers are also located. But the problem itself, unfortunately, does not disappear because of this.

But how often does the domestic audience remember these facts? No, and there is nothing to blame it for — the new wave of pressure on Telegram began without proper public and media coverage, as if out of nowhere.

❗️As a result, all events surrounding Telegram are now perceived exclusively as a fit of ban-mania without any context. Just like Durov's words about "digital resistance," although it is quite selective and inconsistent.

As for the criminal case itself, one can say this: the fight against Telegram will inevitably end in a thaw, the only question is its form. And so as not to have to glue broken pots later — it is rational simply not to break them unnecessarily.

📡 Spain football chief thanks Iran counterpart for World Cup congratulations

In an official letter to Taj, Louzan Abal expressed appreciation for his “warm congratulations” and said such achievements gain greater meaning when shared with friends and colleagues across the international football community.
​
He also thanked Taj for his friendship and support, expressing hope that the two federations would continue to strengthen their relations.
​
Spain was crowned FIFA World Cup champions for the second time after defeating Argentina 1-0 in extra time in the final at New York New Jersey Stadium on July 19.
